note:
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: bladder cancer, version 3.2026. **`furniture_ends_section` is true for this document, and it is the reason it could be routed at all.** NCCN prints a version banner at `#` on every page while every real chapter is `##`. Dropping the banner as page furniture -- which it plainly is -- left each chapter attached to the last `#` that survived. Here that was `Primary Carcinoma of the Urethra`, holding 156 of the document's 282 passages -- and the urethra is out of scope, so a rule excluding it correctly would have deleted more than half the guideline. It now holds the 5 passages it actually owns. Declaring that the banner ends the section it interrupts puts the chapters back at the root, where a rule can name them.

**The NMIBC rules are stated before the MIBC ones, and the reason is a substring.** NCCN writes `Non–Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer` with an en dash, and `Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer` sits inside it. A rule naming the muscle-invasive disease would claim the non-muscle-invasive chapters first if it came first -- which is the same trap as mCRPC inside nmCRPC, now seen in three documents. Both values are valid, so nothing would have complained.

Like its prostate counterpart, this guideline also documents diseases that are not bladder cancer: upper-tract urothelial carcinoma, the renal pelvis and ureter, and primary carcinoma of the urethra. `out_of_scope_disease` was created for exactly this document.

default.note: The principles chapters -- surgical management, imaging, pathology, systemic therapy -- which are written per modality and cross the disease states.
